data.fix_commit_subject: valid: Don't add ids when validating entity content
data.rationale: The crash chain (xmlIsID ← xmlSAX2AttributeNs ← xmlSAX2StartElementNs) points at ID-table handling during attribute validation in SAX2.c. Commit d53ba0588ef03c910d8956cbfec8a640e528059d (2025-08-23, "valid: Don't add ids when validating entity content", Fixes #974) patches exactly xmlSAX2AttributeNs's validating branch, which previously called xmlValidateOneAttribute -> xmlAddID unconditionally even for attributes inside entity content, leaving the document's ID hash table referencing attribute nodes that get freed once the entity's transient node tree is freed. Later lookups (e.g. via xmlIsID during subsequent attribute processing) then read freed memory, matching a heap-use-after-free read. The fix adds an XML_VCTXT_IN_ENTITY flag set/cleared around the xmlValidateOneAttribute call in both xmlSAX1Attribute and xmlSAX2AttributeNs, and checks it in xmlValidateOneAttribute before calling xmlAddID. It is a single, self-contained commit on master (also cleanly cherry-picked to the 2.13 and 2.14 branches as 5af6f3b6 and 1172b777), landed in v2.14.6/v2.15.0, and is followed by a tiny one-line null-deref regression fix (13962f82) for the same code — but that fix is for a different, self-inflicted regression from this same commit, not the original UAF, so it doesn't need to anchor the differential. Although the given regression_window (2025-08-01 to 2025-08-02) doesn't correspond to any commit touching valid.c/SAX2.c that day, the commit's own message notes the underlying root cause was introduced much earlier (d025cfbb, Dec 2023) — regression windows for long-dormant fuzzer-discovered bugs often reflect fuzz-target/corpus changes rather than the true introducing commit, and I was instructed not to hunt for the introducing commit. The code-path match to the crash_state is precise and this is the only commit found that touches SAX2AttributeNs's ID-registration logic in this timeframe.

data.note: Rescanned after broadening the FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION fix from a fixed-asan-only local patch to a permanent harness/build.sh change (both release-asan and fixed-asan rebuilt from the corrected script). fixed-asan is now fully clean (0/34015). The 27 remaining vuln-asan-only crashes (19 timeout/hang, 7 ABRT, both pre-existing and unrelated to this bug -- see handle_corpus_anomaly) plus this bug's own 1 UAF crash are expected per SOP: pre-existing unrelated bugs on the vuln side don't block shipping as long as fixed-asan is clean.

data.root_cause:
The fixed-asan oracle is genuinely dirty against the historical `reader` corpus, but the cause is unrelated to the id/entity fix (d53ba0588e) itself: our harness/build.sh never defines `FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION`, the macro real OSS-Fuzz always passes for libxml2 builds. Dozens of `#ifdef FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION` guards throughout libxml2 (xinclude.c, xpath.c, ...) exist specifically to bound pathological XPath/XPointer work reachable via `<xi:include xpointer="...">`; without them they're compiled out.

Confirmed by rebuilding libxml2 at the exact fix_commit from scratch (cmake+clang, ASAN) and reproducing both symptom classes with a debug/verbose harness:
1. 17 "summary: null" entries are wall-clock hangs, not crashes. Forcing a SIGSEGV mid-hang (via an alarm handler) and symbolizing the stack showed unbounded recursive re-evaluation in xmlXPathNodeCollectAndTest/xmlXPathCompOpEvalToBoolean/xmlXPathNodeSetFilter, entered from xmlTextReaderRead -> xmlXIncludeProcessNode -> xmlXIncludeLoadDoc -> xmlXPtrEval, triggered by documents containing `<xi:include ... xpointer="xpointer(...*[///*[...)"/>`. xinclude.c normally caps this via `ctxt->xpctxt->opLimit = 100000` and a 20-inclusion `incTotal` cap, but both are wrapped in `#ifdef FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION` and thus inactive in our build.
2. The 2 "AddressSanitizer: ABRT" entries symbolize (via addr2line on the unstripped fixed-asan binary) to `xmlFuzzCheckFailureReport` at fuzz/reader.c:542 — the harness's own malloc-failure-injection self-check aborting because a simulated OOM wasn't (or was erroneously) reflected as `XML_ERR_NO_MEMORY` on the reader's last error. Same code path (xinclude/xpointer via a similar `xi:include xpointer=...` document); with far more allocations happening per run due to the missing op-limit, the harness's fixed "fail at the Nth malloc" position drifts into allocation-count-sensitive corners of the OOM-report bookkeeping.

Verification: defining `FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION` for the whole library build makes all 7 given crashing hashes (and a random 400-file sample of the 34k-file corpus) run clean (exit 0) on a from-scratch ASAN rebuild at the fix_commit. Isolated partial fixes (only xinclude.c's opLimit/incTotal) killed the 5 hangs but left the 2 ABRT cases failing, confirming the ABRT class depends on other FUZZING_BUILD_MODE-gated allocation-size guards elsewhere (xpath.c's maxStep/valueMax=1 sizing, etc.) rather than being a distinct bug.
data.notes:
Root cause is a benchmark-harness build gap, not a libxml2 regression from the fix commit itself, and definitely not part of xmlisid-attribute-uaf's own fix (SAX2.c/valid.c/include/private/parser.h are untouched by this patch). The patch adds a 1-line `#define FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION` (guarded with `#ifndef`) to libxml.h, the private header included by virtually every libxml2 .c file, exactly reproducing the macro real OSS-Fuzz always defines for this project. This is the single smallest change that activates every relevant guard at once (op-limits, inclusion caps, allocation-size tuning, deterministic hash/dict seeding) instead of hand-picking individual `#ifdef` sites, which I verified was insufficient (still left 2/7 crashing).

I did check for an existing upstream commit that might have "fixed" this instead (there is a real, confirmed 1-day regression in d53ba0588e itself — a NULL deref in xmlValidateOneAttribute, fixed the next day by upstream commit 13962f82 "Short-lived regression from d53ba058") but that path is never reached by this specific `reader` fuzz target (xmlValidateOneAttribute's `ctxt` is always `&parserCtxt->vctxt`, never NULL, from SAX2.c's callers), and it does not explain any of the crashes actually observed in the corpus, so I did not fold it into this patch — it's unrelated to what's actually failing here.

I did not run the full 34k-file corpus (too slow one-file-per-process-launch within tool timeouts); I validated all 7 given example hashes plus a random 400-file sample, all clean.

CORRECTION after initial diagnosis: applying this fix as a local patch to fixed-asan ONLY would have been wrong -- the missing macro affects vuln-asan identically (both builds showed similar hang/ABRT counts pre-fix), so patching only fixed-asan would have left vuln-asan alone still hang-prone on unrelated xi:include XPath-bomb inputs while fixed-asan was clean, creating a spurious differential-positive risk (crash-on-vuln/no-crash-on-fixed for an unrelated, non-existent 'bug'). The actual fix applied was instead a permanent addition of -DFUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION to harness/build.sh's CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS for the library build (both release-asan and fixed-asan variants use the same script), matching what real OSS-Fuzz always defines for this project. No local tools/fixes/ patch file was needed or kept. Re-verified: release-asan still reproduces the target UAF; fixed-asan is fully clean against the full 34015-file corpus.

scrub_decision.keep_reasoning:
NEWS is libxml2's changelog/release-notes file. It contains a direct answer leak at line 2357: "Heap use-after-free in xmlSAX2AttributeNs (Pranjal Jumde)" under the "2.9.4: May 23 2016 - Security" section, which names one of this bug's own crash functions verbatim. The file also contains thousands of other historical bug/CVE-style entries (SAX2 leaks, memory errors, overflow fixes, etc.) spanning the whole project history that would serve as decoy leads for a solver. This matches the judgement rule for deletion (changelog/release-notes record of past bugs naming crash functions or serving as decoys).

The other name-sweep candidates were inspected and are NOT changelogs of past project defects:
- test/schemas/changelog093_0.xml, test/schemas/changelog093_1.xsd, result/schemas/changelog093_1_0.err: XML Schema test fixtures using a fictional "http://www.blackperl.com/XML/ChangeLog" namespace for identity-constraint testing — unrelated to libxml2's own bug history.
- test/valid/dtds/NewsMLv1.2.dtd: a DTD for the NewsML 1.2 news-industry XML format, unrelated to libxml2 release history.

content_sweep found no README/*.md/*.txt with CVE/security-advisory phrasing, so nothing there to delete.
